output.title: What seasonality hides in a small business workflow
output.body:
Seasonality can hide a workflow problem, not just a sales pattern. If your numbers swing by month, it is easy to miss the work that still repeats all year: customer questions, invoice handling, or data reconciliation. Those jobs do not disappear in the slow months. They just get harder to see.

The practical question is simple: which single recurring task keeps showing up whether demand is high or low, and still gets handled manually? Do not start with the biggest mess. Start with the one task that has the clearest handoff, the clearest input, and the clearest definition of “done.”

If you can name 2–3 candidates, pick the one where you can point to a real output: an approved reply, a checked invoice, a cleaned record, or a passed-to-human decision. That is the kind of task worth testing for AI support.

A good next step is a short diagnostic that maps the workflow end to end and checks whether it is truly year-round. If it only appears in peak season, leave it alone for now. If it persists quietly under the seasonal noise, that is where a bounded automation conversation starts. No mystery, just a better filter.
